Who are we?

FalconX is a pioneering team of operators, investors, and builders committed to revolutionizing institutional access to the crypto markets. Operating at the intersection of traditional finance and  cutting-edge technology, FalconX addresses the industry's foremost challenges: Navigating the digital asset market can be complex and fragmented, with limited products and services that support trading strategies, structures, and liquidity found in conventional financial markets. As a comprehensive solution for all digital asset strategies from start to scale, FalconX operates as the connective tissue empowering clients with seamless navigation through the ever- evolving cryptocurrency landscape.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on Chartered Accountant with strong derivatives experience to run day-to-day accounting, product control, and financial reporting for our U.S. NFA/CFTC-regulated swap dealer and our international subsidiaries.

You'll work across both Product Control and Legal Entity Control. Your work will include daily derivative MTM and P&L, balance sheet close, and statutory reporting. You'll work closely with the Finance Manager, Front-Office Trading Desks, and Trade Operations, and help automate our processes in NetSuite.

What You'll Do

  1. Entity Accounting & Financial Close
  • Run monthly, quarterly, and annual close tasks under US GAAP and IFRS for the U.S. swap dealer entity and operating subsidiaries. This covers journal entries, accruals, intercompany eliminations, and balance sheet reconciliations.
  • Prepare balance sheet schedules and first drafts of statutory financial statements and footnote disclosures for the Manager to review. Disclosures include gross/net offsetting (ASC 210-20 / IFRS 7), fair value levels (ASC 820 / IFRS 13), and credit risk.
  • Monitor and settle intercompany balances, and support transfer pricing calculations, including intercompany crypto and derivative positions.
  1. Product Control & Derivatives Accounting
  • Run daily mark-to-market (MTM) and P&L for OTC and exchange-traded derivatives. Products include BTC/ETH options, systematic OTC trades, funded collars, total return swaps, interest rate swaps (IRS), and FX forwards.
  • Produce daily P&L attribution, explain P&L movements to Trading Desks, and investigate breaks with Trade Operations.
  • Support fair value leveling (Level 1–3), Expected Credit Loss (ECL) calculations, and margin and collateral reconciliations.
  • Research and draft accounting assessments (ASC 815 / IFRS 9) for new products such as digital asset lending, borrowing, staking, and principal market-making.
  1. Audit, Controls & Regulatory Support
  • Act as a day-to-day contact for Big 4 external auditors. Prepare PBC (provided-by-client) schedules, answer audit queries, and build historical workpapers.
  • Carry out legacy balance sheet cleanups and help draft technical GAAP position memos.
  • Run and document key controls under SOX 404 / ICFR, and keep Risk Control Matrices (RCMs) and SOPs up to date.
  • Provide financial data for regulatory and capital reporting under NFA, CFTC, and SEC rules and other global regimes, working with Compliance.
  1. Process Improvement & Team Support
  • Find manual spreadsheet workflows that can be automated, and help move them into NetSuite reporting.
  • Mentor and review the work of 1–2 junior associates or analysts.

What You Bring

Must-Have

  • Qualified Chartered Accountant (ICAI).
  • 5-8 years of experience in Product Control or Legal Entity Control at a Tier-1 investment bank (e.g., Goldman Sachs, Barclays, StanChart, BofA, Morgan Stanley), or in Big 4 Capital Markets / Financial Services audit or advisory.
  • Hands-on derivatives experience: daily MTM, P&L attribution, fair value measurement, and margin and collateral for OTC and/or exchange-traded derivatives.
  • Experience preparing balance sheet reconciliations, close schedules, and statutory disclosure schedules.
  • Strong working knowledge of US GAAP and IFRS, especially:
    • Derivatives: ASC 815 / IFRS 9
    • Fair value: ASC 820 / IFRS 13
    • Offsetting and disclosures: ASC 210 / IFRS 7
  • Advanced MS Excel skills and hands-on ERP experience (NetSuite preferred, or Oracle or SAP).
  • Based in Bengaluru, or willing to relocate, for a 3-day in-office hybrid schedule.

Good-to-Have

  • CPA, ACCA, or CFA (any level).
  • Exposure to crypto or digital asset accounting (ASC 350-60, IAS 38 / IAS 2) or crypto derivatives (perpetuals, funding rates).
  • Experience with SOX/ICFR controls 
  • Familiarity with crypto accounting tools (e.g., Bitwave, SoftLedger, Ledgible) or blockchain explorers.

How You Work

  • Detail-oriented and reliable, with strong analysis and problem-solving skills.
  • Clear communicator who can explain P&L and accounting positions to Traders, Operations, and auditors.
  • Keen to grow into a Manager role and to learn about digital assets and derivatives.

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform.

We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work.

 

The opportunity

  • Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference.

  • Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks.

  • Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete.

  • Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises.

  • Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance.

  • Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams.

  • Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions.

  • Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production.

 

What you bring

  • 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time.

  • Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns.

  • Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. You can explain the mechanisms and diagnostic evidence behind your decisions.

  • Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain.

  • Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Rust or a comparable language. You have personally built and maintained production software or automation for database workflows such as provisioning, failover, online schema changes and self-service operations, using version control, code review and delivery pipelines, with tested failure handling.

  • Strong low-level Linux, Kernel, storage and networking fundamentals, with the ability to investigate problems beyond the database process.

  • Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery.

 

Nice to haves

  • Experience operating databases in containerised, hybrid on-premises/cloud or multi-region environments. Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code or GitOps, including their operational trade-offs.

  • Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar).

  • Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch.

  • Experience in regulated environments or contributions to database engines, operators and other infrastructure software.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Ramp is building the future of work with AI. We’re bringing a new class of AI-native products to market that can understand business context, make decisions, and increasingly execute work on behalf of customers.

We’re looking for an AI Account Executive to help build the commercial motion for this emerging portfolio. You’ll own the full sales cycle, from creating pipeline and shaping the customer’s problem through evaluation, close, and activation. You’ll work across Engineering, IT, Security, and Procurement to turn complex AI capabilities into clear business outcomes.

This is a founding seller role. You’ll help define the market, qualification criteria, sales process, messaging, and playbooks that the broader organization will use. The right person is both a closer and a builder: someone who can win important early customers, learn quickly from the field, and turn those lessons into a repeatable system. We’re hiring AI Account Executives at multiple levels. The scope of the role, title, and compensation will reflect your experience and demonstrated ability to lead complex sales cycles and build new commercial motions.

  • Own the full sales cycle: Source, qualify, develop, and close net-new opportunities for Ramp’s AI products, with accountability for pipeline creation, revenue, and forecast accuracy.

  • Create demand in an emerging category: Help customers identify high-value AI use cases, connect technical capabilities to urgent business problems, and build conviction before a mature buying process exists.

  • Navigate complex buying groups. Multi-thread across Finance, Engineering, IT, Security, Procurement, and executive stakeholders to align technical requirements, economic value, and organizational priorities.

  • Turn field learning into a playbook: Document repeatable qualification criteria, buyer patterns, use cases, proof points, and deal strategies that improve the performance of future sellers.

  • Influence the product roadmap: Build a tight feedback loop with Product and Engineering by clearly communicating what customers value, where deals stall, and which capabilities will unlock adoption.

  • Operate as a founding team member: Help establish the standards, culture, tooling, and operating cadence for Ramp’s AI sales organization.

What you need

  • A track record of meeting or exceeding revenue targets in complex B2B software sales, whether you’re an experienced AE ready for a new challenge or a seasoned enterprise seller looking to build something new.

  • Experience owning multi-stakeholder sales cycles from pipeline generation through close, ideally involving six-figure contracts or enterprise customers.

  • Demonstrated success selling a new product, emerging category, or technical solution without relying on a fully established playbook.

  • Strong discovery and business-case development skills, including the ability to quantify ROI, total cost of ownership, and measurable operational outcomes.

  • Technical fluency and intellectual curiosity: you can credibly discuss integrations, data flows, security, reliability, and AI capabilities with technical stakeholders without resorting to hand-waving.

  • Executive presence and the ability to communicate clearly with CFOs, CTOs, Finance leaders, Engineering teams, Procurement, and Security.

About Us

Established in 2018, Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges and digital financial platforms, serving over 80 million users across more than 200 countries and regions. Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance.
 
Our core values define how we build. We listen, care and improve to create products and experiences that put users first. Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution.

About the Role

The Compliance Operations Specialist supports the day-to-day execution of Bybit's global compliance operations programme.
Working across multiple licensed jurisdictions, you will help ensure regulatory commitments are translated into practical operating processes, tracked effectively, and maintained throughout the licence lifecycle. This role works closely with Legal, Licensing, Product, Operations and regional teams to support operational readiness and ongoing compliance activities.

Responsibilities

  • Manage the tracking of regulatory obligations, licensing conditions and operational actions, coordinating with stakeholders to ensure timely completion.
  • Coordinate the operational implementation of new licences, including developing SOPs, implementation checklists and business readiness materials in collaboration with relevant stakeholders
  • Monitor adherence to compliance operational processes, proactively identifying, managing and escalating risks or overdue actions.
  • Prepare operational reports, implementation updates and management briefing materials for senior stakeholders.
  • Coordinate cross-functional regulatory implementation activities with Legal, Licensing, Product, Operations and regional teams.
  • Support audits, regulatory inspections and operational reviews by coordinating documentation, evidence gathering and remediation tracking.
  • Conduct operational gap assessments, identify areas for improvement and drive remediation initiatives to strengthen compliance processes and controls.

Requirements

  • 2 - 4 years experience in Compliance Operations, Regulatory Operations, Project Management Office or a similar operational role within financial services, fintech or another regulated industry.
  • Experience coordinating cross-functional projects or operational initiatives, working with stakeholders across different functions and jurisdictions
  • Strong organisational and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams, follow through on deliverables and work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to develop clear SOPs, process documentation and management reports.
  • Comfortable working independently in a fast-paced environment with competing priorities.

  • Highly organised with strong follow-through and execution discipline.
  • Proactive, dependable and solution-oriented.

The 4 biggest blockchain strengths are also its weakness

  • Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

  • Decentralization leads to too many standards

  • Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

  • Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.

Blockchains are optimized for writes, not reads.

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

  • Fragmented standards

  • Exponential complexity

  • No accountability for interpretation

  • Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.

Allium is building the System of Record for Onchain Finance

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

  • Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

  • Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

  • Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

  • Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.

Finance is moving onchain

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability.

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

Who We Serve

Allium powers three core personas with the same canonical data foundation:

1. Finance, Accounting, and Risk Teams They need reliable, audit grade answers. They rely on Allium for financial reporting, reconciliation, compliance, risk monitoring, and defensible metrics that can stand up to auditors and regulators.

2. Engineers and Product Teams They need low latency, production ready infrastructure. They use Allium to power wallets, trading systems, payment rails, staking infrastructure, and real time applications that cannot break.

3. Strategy, Research, and Executive Teams They need clarity and insight. They use Allium to understand ecosystem economics, market structure, user behavior, competitive dynamics, and where capital is flowing onchain.

And of course...agents 🦞. Our customers and users include Visa, Stripe, G-SIB Banks, Big 4 Accounting firms, BCG, Coinbase, Phantom, Uniswap and cited by the Federal Reserve.

About the role

About the team

Stripe’s Accounting Products team is building modern infrastructure for the Office of the CFO. Our vision is to give finance teams, and the agents that support them, one reconciled and explainable presentation of financial truth.

Today, the data and context required to make accounting decisions are fragmented across billing systems, contracts, spreadsheets, general ledgers, and the minds of the people doing the work. Finance teams spend significant time reconstructing what happened, determining the appropriate accounting treatment, reconciling results, and gathering evidence. Giving an agent access to the underlying data is not enough: it also needs the business context, accounting policies, approved judgments, and guardrails required to act reliably.

Revenue Recognition is our first major proof point. Stripe has a unique opportunity to help Billing and Metronome users turn complex revenue activity—including usage-based pricing, minimum commitments, credits, and contract modifications—into accurate, explainable journal entries. Our ambition is for agents to take on the investigation, configuration, and repetitive work while accountants retain control over consequential judgments and approvals.

Over time, we expect to expand into additional Office of the CFO workflows, and we are looking for a Staff Product Manager to help turn this vision into products that finance teams trust. This is a senior individual contributor role with significant ownership, autonomy, and influence across Product, Engineering, Design, Finance, Data Science, and Go-to-Market teams.

What you’ll do

You’ll own a significant product area within Accounting Products, setting its strategy, roadmap, and measures of success. You’ll translate the broader product vision into a focused plan, taking it from customer discovery and early prototypes through scaled adoption.

You’ll help build the future of agentic accounting: products that help finance teams automate work, understand financial results, and resolve exceptions while retaining control. Your work will connect Stripe’s Revenue Suite with the external systems customers rely on to manage their accounting workflows.

  • Take products from prototype to scale with design partners, deciding what to standardize, automate, or keep narrow, and define integrations with general ledgers, ERP, customer relationship management, and professional-services platforms

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of product management experience delivering complex, technically or domain-intensive products, including as a senior individual contributor who independently sets direction, aligns cross-functional teams, and drives decisions without formal authority
  • Experience building products for finance, accounting, or similarly demanding domains where accuracy, controls, traceability, and trust are essential, with a high bar for correctness, explainability, reliability, and operability
